title: Principal Product Manager, Graph & Reporting
description: Veeam is the Data and AI Trust Company, specializing in helping organizations ensure their data and AI are fully understood, secured, and resilient to enable the acceleration of safe AI at scale. As the market leader in both data resilience and data security posture management, Veeam is built for the convergence of identity, data, security, and AI risk. Headquartered in Seattle with offices in more than 30 countries, Veeam protects over 550,000 customers worldwide, who trust Veeam to keep their businesses running. Join us as we go fearlessly forward together, growing, learning, and making a real impact for some of the world’s biggest brands. About the Role You will own product for the Knowledge Graph and the reporting and analytics experience inside Veeam Data Command Platform (DSPM and AISPM). The graph is where the product's intelligence lives: what sensitive data exists, who can access it, how it moves, and whether the AI working on it can be governed. Actionable dashboards and reporting are how customers see that intelligence, prove their posture to auditors and executives, and decide — and act on — what to fix first.   This is a builder's product role. You will translate a complex graph data model into queries, views, dashboards, and evidence that security, privacy, and governance teams use every day — and you will partner closely with the engineering leader who owns the graph platform and hyperscale lake integrations.   You will set the roadmap, define the metrics that matter, and work AI-first — using agentic tools to prototype, analyze, and ship faster than a traditional PM team.   What You’ll Do Own the product vision and roadmap for the Knowledge Graph as a customer-facing capability: the entities, relationships, and insights customers can explore, query, and trust. Partner with engineering on the underlying data modeling (sources, identities, access, classifications, lineage) and translate those decisions into concepts customers actually understand   Own the dashboard experience end to end: default landing views per persona (CISO, privacy, data governance, security operations), what earns a spot on them, and the path from a top-line number to underlying records in a few clicks. Every widget should answer "so what do I do now?", letting a user assign an owner, open a ticket, launch remediation, tighten a permission, or apply a policy without leaving the view   Own the widget framework and library (posture scores, top risks, sensitive-data heatmaps, access exposure, AI usage, trend lines) with consistent filtering, time ranges, and drill-through. Enable customization and role-based layouts so customers and internal teams can build, save, share, and default dashboards by role or business unit   Define the reporting layer: a report builder with saved/shared views, scheduling and subscriptions, and export in the formats enterprises use (PDF, CSV, API). Own audit and evidence packages that hold up for regulators and auditors, with clear scope, timestamps, and provenance back to the graph, and extend reporting coverage to backup and archive estates (Veeam Data Cloud workloads: Microsoft 365, Entra ID, Salesforce) so posture and evidence reflect historical data, not just production   Drive trending and posture-over-time reporting, including alerting and thresholds, so customers can show risk reduction rather than a single snapshot. Set the bar for data quality and freshness: how recent the numbers are, how coverage gaps are disclosed, and how the product avoids reporting false confidence   Enable downstream and agent consumption: BI integration, warehouse export, and APIs for customers who want the data in their own stack, plus partnering with the AI Agents team to expose graph queries, findings, and posture metrics as MCP tools and resources for customer and internal AI agents   Turn graph traversals into product surfaces: access paths, blast radius, data flow/lineage views, AI exposure, and risk prioritization. Partner with the Access Entitlements team on identity-to-data surfaces (multi-hop reachability through nested groups and shadow roles, least-privilege recommendations, entitlements for non-human identities). Own query and search UX for non-technical users, including natural-language and AI-assisted question answering over the graph, and define scale/performance requirements from the user's point of view (what must return in under a second, what can be async, where multi-hop queries must stay interactive at enterprise scale), holding the bar with engineering   Build the metrics and KPI framework the platform reports on, aligned with regulatory and framework mappings customers are measured against. title: Agentic Operations Architect
description: About Gusto At Gusto, we're on a mission to grow the small business economy. We handle the hard stuff — payroll, health insurance, 401(k)s, and HR — so owners can focus on their craft and their customers. With teams in Denver, San Francisco, and New York, we support more than 500,000 small businesses nationwide and are building a workplace that reflects the people we serve.   All full-time employees receive competitive base pay, benefits, and equity (RSUs) — because everyone who helps build Gusto should share in its success. Offer amounts are determined by role, level, and location. Learn more about our Total Rewards philosophy .   AI is a fundamental part of how work gets done at Gusto. We expect all team members to actively engage with AI tools relevant to their role and grow their fluency as the technology evolves. AI experience requirements vary by role and will be assessed during the interview process. About the Role: As an Agentic Operations Architect, you will own the reusable capabilities that make agentic service workflows possible, the patterns, primitives, standards, and tooling that other builders across the org use to automate discrete customer problems. You are not the owner of any single workflow. You are the reason a workflow that took six weeks takes two, and the reason the tenth one is safer than the first. You will prototype workflows yourself, but as a means to an end: to prove a pattern is sound, to find out what builders are missing, and to earn the right to set a standard. About the Team: The mission of our Service Transformation (CXT) team is to quickly evolve and scale how Gusto delivers outstanding service experiences and leverages AI to do so. Our team designs the systems, governance frameworks, and feedback loops that allow Gusto's service model to improve continuously, operate reliably, and earn the trust of the customers and employees who depend on it. Here’s what you’ll do day-to-day: Build the patterns Design the reusable patterns for agentic service workflows, orchestration, HITL protocols, override and escalation logic, quality safeguards, so builders assemble from proven components Set the standards builders work to, concrete enough to apply without you in the room Prototype workflows selectively: to validate a pattern, expose a gap, or unblock a hard problem, then extract the reusable part and hand it off Pull learnings from every build back into the shared patterns, so each one is faster and safer than the last Shape the platform Influence Product on what to build next: turn what's slowing builders down into specific, prioritized asks backed by evidence Prototype around gaps the platform doesn't cover yet, proving a capability is worth building before USP invests Be honest in both directions about the distance between what builders need and what exists Point capacity at the right problems Rank automation opportunities by volume, risk, and customer impact, mining SOPs, operational metrics, and interaction data, to determine what gets built and where builders go Work with Data to define how workflow performance gets measured, so every builder measures the same way Identify where there are processes which exist which should not be automated Carry the quality stakes Bring what's at stake for customers into Legal, Security, Compliance, and platform reviews, so requirements land in the patterns instead of getting retrofitted per workflow Represent how the portfolio is performing to senior stakeholders, briefly, and in a way that drives action Here’s what we're looking for: 8+ years in operations, product, or AI roles — with at least 2 years designing and deploying AI-assisted or agentic workflows in production Hands-on experience with agentic tooling, orchestration frameworks, or MCP-style integrations, including multi-agent coordination — conceptual familiarity is not sufficient at this level Strong fluency with LLM systems: prompt design, evaluation, and how models actually behave at scale Experience designing human-in-the-loop systems with clear escalation logic, override controls, and compliance-aware checkpoints Ability to define and diagnose workflow metrics — solve and assist rate, containment, escalation quality — and to tell a real regression from noise Proven track record optimization Ability to assess whether underlying data structures, quality, and governance can support reliable agentic performance Experience in SaaS, fintech, or regulated environments where
